clue.text: All-round sportsmen in Japan may be experts in this

definitions.text: sportsmen in Japan may be experts in this

parts.note: the sum is the total, the whole lot, so all gives SUM
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that Japanese athletes may be good at every sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-round' reads as one word meaning versatile, but it splits: All gives SUM, round gives O. The definition then points at the heavyweight wrestling of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the traditional Japanese wrestling sport, so its wrestlers are Japanese sportsmen expert in it.

clue.text: Most alert breed of dog briefly spotted on street

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the dog breed loses its last letter

parts.note: the shar-pei is a wrinkly Chinese dog breed

explanation.surface: A very watchful dog seen out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharpest person is the keenest and quickest-witted.

clue.text: Study of religion in place of worship that's Moorish in style

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the place of worship

parts.note: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship
RE is religious education, the school subject

explanation.surface: Religious studies held in a Moorish-style building.
explanation.definitionFit: Moresque describes decoration in the manner of the Moors, as in Spanish Islamic architecture.

clue.text: Tom's gang displaying instrument of torture

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so Tom's gives THUMB'S
a gang of workers is a crew

explanation.surface: A boy's band of friends shows off a torture device.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb, the thumb-sized boy of English folk tale, supplies the first part; the apostrophe S stays as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbscrew was a device for crushing the thumbs, used to extract confessions.

clue.text: About to run out of liquor: that'll lead to a row

indicators.note: something that runs out of a container leaves it, so the letter for about is taken from the liquor

parts.note: hooch is slang for liquor, especially illicit or cheap spirits
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the drink is nearly gone, which will cause an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOCH loses its C (circa, about) to leave HOOH; then 'that'll lead to' links to A and the definition 'row'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or commotion, the noisy kind of row people make over something.

clue.text: Brand name on dress hastily put together

parts.note: the make of a product is its brand name
a shift is a simple loose-fitting dress

explanation.surface: A designer label on a frock that was sewn in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a temporary, improvised substitute thrown together for the moment.

clue.text: Unexpectedly brusque about beginning

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Unexpectedly brusque about beginning (12)'; the blog parses SUR(P RISING)LY, but no word in the clue as held gives P RISING, so a word or more is missing.

clue.text: Problem: no time to get money for trip abroad

indicators.note: no here says the letter for time is absent, taken out of the word for problem

parts.note: trouble is a problem or difficulty

explanation.surface: A traveller frets that a lack of time is a problem for getting currency for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency of Russia, so it is money a traveller there would need.

clue.text: Not dirty money woman stashed away

indicators.note: something stashed away is tucked inside, so the woman goes inside the money

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman has hidden away some laundered cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not dirty money' looks like one phrase for laundered cash, but 'Not dirty' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been washed are clean, the opposite of soiled.

clue.text: Off for a hairdo

indicators.note: off as in gone off or out of order, so the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to get their hair done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as departing, but it is the anagram signal on FOR A.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a hairstyle of tight curls forming a full rounded shape.

clue.text: What rock festival organisers do for those knowledgeable about volume?

definitions.meaning: promoters hire and schedule bands for the stage
a reading circle whose members have all read the same book

explanation.surface: A question about festival bookers and people who know a lot about loudness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like loudness at a rock gig, but it means a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Festival promoters engage bands for their line-up; reading clubs meet to discuss a chosen volume.

clue.text: Views enjoyed by all in Wimbledon area?

definitions.meaning: opinions or points of agreement shared by everyone
Wimbledon Common, the public open land of that London district

explanation.surface: Shared opinions placed on a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon Common is a large open public space in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed points shared by both sides of a debate; also land open to the whole community, like Wimbledon's.

clue.text: Pictures of rural life used in history exams

parts.note: history is the past
orals are spoken examinations

explanation.surface: Paintings of the countryside set as questions in history exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral works portray shepherds and idyllic country scenes.

clue.text: German poet readers primarily like in translation

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of readers is used
translating rearranges the language, so the letters of the word like are rearranged

explanation.surface: Readers mostly enjoy a German poet once translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke wrote the Duino Elegies in German.

clue.text: Female must find us full of excitement

definitions.text: Female must find us full of excitement

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and agitated, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The hunks say a woman is bound to find them thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: F plus the letters of MUST FIND US rearranged; the whole clue is also the definition, spoken by the sexy men themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud muffins are attractive, sexy men, whom a woman would find exciting.

clue.text: Reach an understanding of one, maybe, abroad

parts.note: one is an example of a figure, a numeral
abroad means out of doors, out and about

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps overseas, comes to grasp something.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or solve a problem is to come to comprehend it.

clue.text: Make the most of saw: cut ends off part of staircase

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim

indicators.note: cutting off both ends removes the first and last letters of the step part

parts.note: a riser is the vertical part of a stair step

explanation.surface: A carpenter plans to use the saw well, trimming the edges of a stair part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is the tool in the surface but means a saying here.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to get the greatest possible benefit from it.

clue.text: City announced beauty queen's rating

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: a belle is a beauty and a grade is a rating, giving belle grade

explanation.surface: The judges reveal the marks a beauty pageant winner scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia.

clue.text: Evening at home with good beer and a bird

parts.note: the evening is night time
someone at home is in
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A cosy evening in with a pint and some birdwatching.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird famous for singing after dark.

clue.text: Shows sympathy-not half!- for Gordon Ramsay's assistant

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, so its first six letters are used

parts.note: someone who commiserates expresses sympathy

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef's helper is very sympathetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it literally takes half of COMMISERATES. Gordon Ramsay is a famous British TV chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A commis chef is a junior cook working under a senior chef in a professional kitchen.

clue.text: Italian family, one welcomed by Garbo excitedly

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by a host is taken in, so one goes inside
excited letters jump around and are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo greets an Italian family member with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges GARBO into BORGA, and 'welcomed by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Borgias were a powerful Renaissance dynasty that produced popes and the notorious Lucrezia.

clue.text: Occasion in court when extremists are ejected, causing a stink

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, the occasion sitting within the trimmed court
the extremists of a word are its outer letters, ejected to leave the middle

parts.note: a do is a party or occasion

explanation.surface: A court hearing where radicals are thrown out causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists are ejected' sounds like a courtroom scene, but it trims the outer letters of court; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad smell is an unpleasant scent, which a stink is.

clue.text: Remembering occupation by military group

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a calling is a vocation or occupation

explanation.surface: Thinking back to when the army occupied a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests a military takeover, but it means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalling a past event is bringing it back to mind.

clue.text: Boorish type caught having fling

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to fling something is to hurl it

explanation.surface: A lout is caught having a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests a romance, but it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a rude, ill-mannered person.

clue.text: Virgil's great work

parts.note: great work rendered in Latin, the language the Roman poet wrote in

explanation.surface: The Aeneid, the masterpiece of the Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's means 'as Virgil would say it', in Latin, not the poem he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece, the most important piece of an artist's career, is called this Latin phrase.

clue.text: Unnatural desire created by film aimed at adults in the 1950s

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
A was the old British film certificate for adult-oriented films

explanation.surface: A risque 1950s film gave rise to a perverse craving.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British film ratings ran U (universal), A (adult) and X; the A rating existed in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a medical condition, a craving to eat things that are not food such as chalk or soil.

clue.text: Traffic jam maybe creates problem on one street and another

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
another street, so a second ST
ill as a noun is a problem or trouble

explanation.surface: Gridlock causes trouble on one road after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam on the roads brings vehicles to a complete halt, the example given.

clue.text: International snap election held

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the run of words snap election

explanation.surface: A sudden election is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' is a noun: a player capped for his country, here the great Brazilian footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelé played for Brazil, winning three World Cups.
